newsitem.title: FINLAND: Wall St swing carries Helsinki back to life-highs.
newsitem.headline: Wall St swing carries Helsinki back to life-highs.

text.p: Shares recouped early losses to scrape another all-time high close on Tuesday after U.S. stocks rebounded at the start, erasing concerns sparked by an overnight slide and fuelling a late burst of buying here, brokers said.
The FOX futures index ended 0.79 percent higher at a life-high 1,087.62, while the HEX closed up 0.65 percent at another life high of 3,178.33 points.
"Yesterday's fall (in the U.S.) had nothing to do with Europe," said one broker, after Finnish stocks recovered with help from a strong opening on Wall Street.
Volume piled up late on to total over 730 million markka.

Even as positive sentiment began to take hold, some brokers warned that another drop in New York would make itself felt all the more strongly here on Wednesday. "That would be a whole new ball game," one said.
Nokia reversed early losses caused by overnight U.S. weakness to end 3.00 markka higher at 380.00 in sturdy 250 million markka volume.
Brokers were again looking for Nokia to test 400.00 markka, possibly quite soon if U.S. strength holds.
Steel group Rautaruukki gained 1.70 to 52.80 in hefty 15 million markka trade.
One broker said Rautaruukki had broken through a 51.00 markka resistance level, seeing next resistance at 55.00 markka.
Paper machinery maker Valmet rose 1.40 markka to 88.00 in good 42 million markka volume. "It looks like the selling pressure in Valmet has come to an end," one broker said.
Forestries recovered, with the general trend and helped by dollar strength, brokers said. UPM-Kymmene closed 1.50 markka up at 122.00 in heavy 150 million markka volume.
